description: Public content for Cognicopia's activity packets: word search banks, conversation trivia, reminiscence prompts and packet templates. Nothing here is about a real person.

content_payload.framing: An invitation to talk. Every answer is welcome: offer the choices, then follow where the conversation goes.

questions.prompt: Many people danced to rock and roll in the 1950s. Which of these singers is called the King of Rock and Roll?
questions.follow_up: What was a song you liked to dance to?

questions.prompt: The soda shop jukebox was a favorite meeting spot. What did a jukebox play?
questions.follow_up: Who would you go to the soda shop with?

questions.prompt: Which of these was a popular way to hear new songs at home in the 1950s?
questions.follow_up: Which radio program was your family's favorite?

content_payload.framing: Two choices, a clear picture on the page, and all the time in the world. Enjoy the answer together.

questions.prompt: Before refrigerators were common, a block of ice kept food cold in a wooden box. What was the box called?
questions.follow_up: What did your kitchen smell like on a baking day?

questions.prompt: Bread was often made at home. What did a baker use to flatten the dough?
questions.follow_up: Who in the family was the best baker?

content_payload.framing: A conversation starter for a group. Share the choices, then ask who has a favorite film or a favorite song from one.

questions.prompt: Julie Andrews sang on a mountain meadow in a 1965 film. Which film was it?
questions.follow_up: Which song from a movie musical do you still like to hum?

questions.prompt: In 1964, a nanny with an umbrella floated over London. What was her name?
questions.follow_up: Where did you go to see a picture show?

content_payload.print_notes: Largest letters, two directions only, the first letter of each word marked.
Large print, three directions, a word box beside the grid.
Words run in every direction, so the grid keeps a generous margin and heavy letters.

prompts: A summer evening might have meant sitting on the porch. What did you like to do as the day cooled?
Some families kept a garden. What was grown in yours?
Evenings had their own sounds. What was one you liked to hear?
content_payload.facilitator_note: Sit beside the person. Use one prompt at a time and let silence be part of the answer.
